value.body: An electro-technical officer (ETO) is the ship's specialist for electrical and electronic systems — power generation, motors, automation, and navigation and communication equipment. Shipping companies and ship-management firms hire ETOs for merchant vessels. Like other officers, they work on contracts at sea followed by leave ashore.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / diploma in Electrical or Electronics, plus a DG Shipping-approved ETO course

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Contracts at sea followed by leave ashore

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Engineering or diploma graduates in electrical, electronics or related branches complete a DG Shipping-approved ETO pre-sea course, then sail as a trainee ETO before certification and promotion to ETO.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Marine electrical systems and high-voltage safety

value.title: At a glance
items: Months at sea at a stretch, away from family.
Rules on certification come from DG Shipping and the international STCW convention.
Experience can lead to shore roles such as technical superintendent.
